title: Volume Word Problems
short: Find a missing edge or compare containers using volume.
trouble: Students confuse area with volume and give square units for a box's capacity.

blocks.html: You can find volumes of single and combined prisms. In word problems you also work backward to a missing edge, compare containers, and decide which unit makes sense.
Use $V = l \times w \times h$ forward to find a volume, or backward to find a missing edge: divide the volume by the area of the base. Give volumes in cubic units.

If a box holds 120 cubes and its base is $6 \times 4 = 24$ cubes, then the number of layers is $120 \div 24 = 5$. Dividing undoes multiplying. Units tell you what you measured: square units for a flat surface, cubic units for the space inside.

blocks.name: volume
blocks.cap: Build a box with a volume of 24 cubic units. There is more than one way; try another.

blocks.title: A missing edge
blocks.q: A box has a volume of 120 cubic inches. It is 6 inches long and 4 inches wide. How tall is it?

blocks.title: Compare two boxes
blocks.q: Box A is 5 in by 4 in by 3 in. Box B is 6 in by 3 in by 3 in. Which holds more, and by how much?

blocks.title: Bigger cubes
blocks.q: How many 2-cm cubes fit in a box 6 cm by 4 cm by 4 cm?

blocks.html: Giving square units for a box's capacity, such as “45,000 square centimeters” for a fish tank. Capacity is the space inside, so it is counted in cubes. Check the unit: three lengths multiplied give cubic units.
